The completed state aa above leaves that core; the marked family leaves its fixed homogeneous OPE domain; the Wilson maps fail a uniform bound already on the scalar ground. State completion, pole bounds and derived normal support are therefore three independent choices.

Derived scalar change preserves several coefficient constructions without settling those choices. For a differential graded RR-algebra AA, right AA-module MM, left AA-module NN and scalar map R→SR\to S, the two-sided bar proves

(M⊗A𝕃N)⊗R𝕃S≃MS⊗AS𝕃NS. (M\otimes_A^{\mathbb L}N)\otimes_R^{\mathbb L}S \simeq M_S\otimes_{A_S}^{\mathbb L}N_S.

For two right modules, the mapping comparison commutes with scalar change if MM is perfect over AA, or if SS is perfect over RR. The second sufficient condition needs no compactness of MM. In particular RrR_r is perfect over RR, using its two-term resolution; this does not make RsR_s perfect over the singular ring RrR_r, nor justify taking degree-zero endomorphisms before derived reduction. Finite perfect differential-module duals also commute with scalar change, stage by stage for retained pro-duals. Native field realization and closure under the actual relative tensor remain separate requirements.

The centre comparison requires more than these local identities. After descent of the actual physical probe categories and their action functors, and after representability has been established, evaluation gives Zfloc⊗R𝕃S→ZfSlocZ_f^{\mathrm{loc}}\otimes_R^{\mathbb L}S\to Z_{f_S}^{\mathrm{loc}}. Its universality must hold on every allowed SS-probe, including those not already known to be scalar extensions. The relative-probe formulation keeps that condition explicit. Neither the normal vacuum endomorphism calculation nor a separated Wilson gauge proves this physical descent.

From operations to physical states

The local vacuum belongs to the algebra of fields; a prepared state evaluates observables. A scalar augmentation is an operation-preserving map to the scalar algebra, when such a map exists. The empty-configuration unit governs the cut tensor. These four roles must be kept separate even in a free theory. A pole with vacuum coefficient can obstruct a proposed scalar map while the ordinary coefficient algebra still has an augmentation. A field-algebra reconstruction does not, by itself, select an integration cycle or a positive state.

The Wilson construction supplies a physical source and incoming vacuum, together with a supported cap comparison and contact homotopies. Its allowed evaluated extensions have exact finiteness and nilpotence conditions. The Gaussian constructions supply states on specified analytic domains. The gravity comparison requires more: a native action-derived insertion, the allowed local counterterms, a regulator comparison, the determinant line and the normalization that survives sewing. These are separate constructions because each changes what can be evaluated and compared.

The next physical test should distinguish independent descriptions of the same system. A connected correlator or a sewing amplitude is useful when the action, preparation and normalization have already been fixed on both sides. A symmetry that forces a correlator to vanish must be respected in choosing that test. Agreement of a character, an index or a prescribed positive density does not determine the complete state or its dynamics. In an inverse problem one must also ask whether two admitted bulks can have identical retained boundary data. If so, characterizing that ambiguity is part of reconstruction.

Why the other branches are part of the same problem

Hall geometry begins with extensions of objects and their correspondences. Its product is therefore geometrically specified before it is written as a shuffle formula. The cooperation requires its own orientation and Euler factors. The positive current-generated integral comparisons coexist with different ambient lattices; localization can remove a supported obstruction that is present before localization. The missing comparison is an oriented coefficient functor preserving the native product, cooperation, right actions, both moment directions and vacuum, including the normal Gysin operation. The Hall example explains why an exchange ratio alone does not determine that tensor.

The Igusa branch asks for a geometric object whose state space and operations realize modular coefficient data. Parity, root multiplicities and cycle-joining brackets are independent constraints on such an object. A repaired finite-height Lie presentation is useful because it tests those constraints. An all-height replacement with a changed degree-zero quotient asks a different realization question. The Igusa discussion distinguishes the modular index, the proposed state space and the bracket; the equality of the first does not construct the other two.

The mixed holomorphic–topological string branch contributes local field actions, BRST complexes, cyclic structures and open–closed operations. A classical Hamiltonian or an action by derivations need not retain the central term of its quantum Hamiltonian. A regulator must respect the specified local counterterm complex, boundary data and sewing. The quantization discussion keeps the Hamiltonian construction and its central obstruction separate; the state problem asks for the physical insertions and their comparison.

Higher-dimensional examples change the geometry of residues and the cohomological shifts. The Heisenberg system on complex two-dimensional space supplies a polynomial-state coefficient object with a sphere-period operation. It lies outside the uniform diagonal-heart nilpotence hypothesis. The surface construction gives its precise domain, and the derived exchange below provides a further positive operation on a polynomial sector.

Arithmetic examples make the coefficient topology decisive. A bounded division may exist only after a regularity shift; a positive functional on a small test space need not extend to the complete arithmetic domain. The prime-power terms, polar evaluations and archimedean contribution must survive in the same comparison. Finite positivity tests and complex or Tate specializations can miss elements of the intended integral or global object. The arithmetic and global examples identify these differences and the stronger trace-class or positivity statements still needed.

These branches share a demand for operation-preserving comparison, but retain different objects and different deciding tests. A Hall orientation is not a choice of analytic state; a normal collision attachment is not a modular normalization. A completed theory must explain their connections through constructed maps, while retaining the distinctions that the examples force.

Integral shuffle examples retain special-fibre information

The distinction between a generic comparison and integral reconstruction is visible in a small shuffle algebra. The unit lies in A0A_0; the constant polynomial in A1A_1 is a current, not that unit.

Let 𝒞n\mathcal C_n be the span of products of nn currents. It is an ideal of AnA_n. Algebraic families transfer the nilpotent K3 Hall algebra

Hall multiplication can sometimes be compared before a field realization is known. Let SS be a projective K3 surface with an ample class HH and classes D1,D2,D3D_1,D_2,D_3 satisfying H2=8H^2=8, H⋅Di=0H\cdot D_i=0, Di2=−8D_i^2=-8 and Di⋅Dj=−4D_i\cdot D_j=-4 for i≠ji\ne j. Such a lattice and surface exist. The line bundles Li=𝒪S(Di)L_i=\mathcal O_S(D_i) are stable with the same reduced Hilbert polynomial; their self-Ext dimensions are (1,0,1)(1,0,1), and dim⁡Ext⁡1(Li,Lj)=2\dim\operatorname{Ext}^1(L_i,L_j)=2 for i≠ji\ne j, with the other cross-Ext groups zero. Write 𝒜L\mathcal A_L for their category of finite extensions.

Choose an orientation on the three-vertex graph with two arrows between each pair. Add the reverse arrows and impose at each vertex the preprojective moment relation, the signed sum of an arrow followed by its reverse. Let Π̂\widehat\Pi be the completion in the arrow ideal JJ, and let 𝒜Π\mathcal A_\Pi consist of finite-dimensional modules killed by some JNJ^N. Its charge records the three vertex dimensions. The nilpotence requirement makes every infinite formal expression below a finite expression on each object.

For either category the constructible Hall product integrates over actual subobjects using compactly supported Euler characteristic. It evaluates the first function on the quotient and the second on the subobject:

(f*g)(F)=∫U⊂Ff(F/U)g(U)dχc. (f*g)(F)=\int_{U\subset F}f(F/U)g(U)\,d\chi_c.

Here f,gf,g are rational-valued constructible functions on isomorphism classes, and the integral weights their level sets by compactly supported Euler characteristic. The variety parametrizes actual subobjects. Its zero-object indicator is the unit; no Euler characteristic of an automorphism classifying stack is inserted. Let 𝒞Π\mathcal C_\Pi and 𝒞L\mathcal C_L be the subalgebras generated by the vertex-simple and line-bundle indicators, respectively. There is a unique unital charge-graded isomorphism

Θ:𝒞Π→∼𝒞L,eiH↦ℓi. \Theta:\mathcal C_\Pi\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal C_L, \qquad e_i^{\mathrm H}\longmapsto\ell_i.

The construction supplies algebraic families and isomorphisms of the reduced flag varieties used in the convolution. The reason it extends beyond a formal neighborhood is worth making explicit.

The Serre trace gives the Ext category of the LiL_i a strictly unital cyclic minimal model with a perfect pairing of degree −2-2. Its degrees are 0,1,20,1,2, and degree zero consists of the three vertex units. For k≥3k\ge3, an input unit kills mkm_k. An input of degree two forces output degree at least three. If all inputs have degree one, pair the degree-two output with a unit and move that unit into an input by cyclicity. Perfection then forces the output to vanish. Thus only m2m_2 remains. Choose a strictly unital quasi-equivalence 𝖥\mathsf F to the Dolbeault category of the line bundles.

For a module MM killed by JNJ^N, let δM\delta_M be its matrix of arrow-valued Ext classes. The operator

∂‾+βM,βM=∑1≤k<N𝖥kmat(δM,…,δM) \bar\partial+\beta_M, \qquad \beta_M=\sum_{1\le k<N}\mathsf F_k^{\mathrm{mat}}(\delta_M,\ldots,\delta_M)

is integrable by the A∞A_\infty identities. Every omitted term contains a path of length at least NN and is zero. A finite filtration by composition factors proves full faithfulness and exactness, and successive extensions prove essential surjectivity onto the analytic finite-extension category. The functor sends an intertwiner to its original constant matrix on the line-bundle factors. This is an exact equivalence, with all morphisms, rather than only a correspondence between deformation parameters.

Set RN=Π̂/JNR_N=\widehat\Pi/J^N and apply this construction to its left regular module. The resulting analytic bundle has a commuting right RNR_N-action. Projective GAGA algebraizes the bundle and the entire finite-dimensional action, including its multiplication and unit identities. The resulting 𝒫N\mathscr P_N is Zariski locally free of rank one as a right 𝒪S⊗RN\mathcal O_S\otimes R_N-module: a fibrewise cyclic generator extends locally, and the determinant of its regular-module map is invertible near that fibre. Moreover 𝒫N⊗RNRM≅𝒫M\mathscr P_N\otimes_{R_N}R_M\cong\mathscr P_M for M≤NM\le N, coherently in three bounds.

For a finite-type base TT and an RN⊗𝒪TR_N\otimes\mathcal O_T-module 𝒱\mathcal V with locally free vertex summands, the algebraic tensor family is

ΦT(𝒱)=pS*𝒫N⊗RN⊗𝒪S×TpT*𝒱. \Phi_T(\mathcal V) =p_S^*\mathscr P_N\otimes_{R_N\otimes\mathcal O_{S\times T}}p_T^*\mathcal V.

Right local freeness proves exactness, local freeness and arbitrary base change directly. GAGA is used on the fixed projective surface to construct 𝒫N\mathscr P_N; no projectivity assumption is imposed on the family base TT.

Reduced flags determine all words, including their normalization

Fix a reduced variety of nilpotent representations and a sequence of submodule dimensions. Its invariant flag variety is projective over the base. Tensoring its universal flag defines a proper map to the independent iterated Quot scheme of the sheaf family. Take the reduced image. The inverse map evaluates the universal sheaf flag at one point x∈Sx\in S, after a right-module identification 𝒫N(x)≅RN\mathscr P_N(x)\cong R_N. Each resulting subspace is invariant at every closed point; the invariance equations then hold on the reduced base. The two maps are inverse, preserve all subquotients and commute with forgetting or regrouping flags.

Consequently every word in the simple indicators takes the same value on MM and Φ(M)\Phi(M): both values are the Euler characteristic of the same reduced flag variety, read from quotient to subobject. The positive Hall comparison concerns rational constructible functions and their composition subalgebras. Lifting it to critical coefficient complexes requires orientation data and compatibility with every Hall pullback and pushforward, including imaginary operations and primitive parity. An action on an independently defined elliptic state complex requires another correspondence and its zero-length action. Hall Serre identities become state-operator identities only after that action is constructed.

A spherical sheaf gives a complete critical Hall sector

A critical coefficient comparison can be constructed on a different, explicitly specified K3 sector. Fix a smooth projective complex K3 surface SS, an elliptic curve EE with origin, and nonzero volume forms on both. A spherical sheaf here is a nonzero coherent sheaf GG on SS with Hom⁡(G,G)=ℂ\operatorname{Hom}(G,G)=\mathbb C, Ext⁡1(G,G)=0\operatorname{Ext}^1(G,G)=0 and Ext⁡2(G,G)=ℂ\operatorname{Ext}^2(G,G)=\mathbb C. where (ha,hb)(h_a,h_b) sends (x,y,e)(x,y,e) to (thax,thby,e+ha−hb)(t_{h_a}x,t_{h_b}y,e+h_a-h_b). The extra EE records the relative centre. At two zero endpoints the quotient is again BEBE.

Critical normalization includes its automorphism

An oriented critical coefficient is a constructible complex locally obtained from vanishing cycles of a function on a smooth ambient space, glued using a chosen square root of the critical canonical line. It records more than the Euler characteristic of a fibre. Here all coefficients are rational Betti coefficients on complex analytic stacks, and φf=ϕf[−1]\varphi_f=\phi_f[-1], so φ0ℚ=ℚ\varphi_0\mathbb Q=\mathbb Q.

Retain an automorphism as part of the object: write (F,T)(F,T) for a constructible complex with a coherent invertible action generated by TT. τU,f=(−1)dim⁡UMf. \tau_{U,f}=(-1)^{\dim U}M_f.

The distinction is visible for the point presented either by the zero function on a point or by z2z^2 on a line. The second Milnor fibre consists of two points, and a circuit exchanges them, acting by −1-1 on their reduced cohomology. The raw monodromies are therefore +1+1 and −1-1, although the underlying critical lines agree. The dimension sign makes both automorphisms +1+1. This is the convention in Brav–Bussi–Dupont–Joyce–Szendrői, Definition 2.12 and Theorem 6.9, which identifies the glued automorphism with τU,f\tau_{U,f}.

For smooth pullback of relative complex dimension dd, use the explicit rule a†(F,T)=(a*F[d],(−1)da*T[d])a^\dagger(F,T)=(a^*F[d],(-1)^d a^*T[d]). Dimensions add under composition, giving the descent compatibility. The smooth sheaf locus above has zero critical structure: on a smooth identity chart the sheaf of critical sections vanishes. This identifies the critical structure, without identifying arbitrary derived enhancements.

The relative critical coefficient for πn\pi_n removes the absolute coefficient of the common base by tensor inverse:

𝚽n=(ℚℳ¯n[−1],−1),𝚽B−1=(ℚB[1],−1),𝑲n=𝚽n⊗πn*𝚽B−1=(ℚℳ¯n,+1). \begin{aligned} \boldsymbol\Phi_n&=(\mathbb Q_{\overline{\mathcal M}_n}[-1],-1),\\ \boldsymbol\Phi_B^{-1}&=(\mathbb Q_B[1],-1),\\ \boldsymbol K_n&=\boldsymbol\Phi_n\otimes\pi_n^*\boldsymbol\Phi_B^{-1} =(\mathbb Q_{\overline{\mathcal M}_n},+1). \end{aligned}

Thus 𝑲0=(ℚB,+1)\boldsymbol K_0=(\mathbb Q_B,+1) is the unit. Merely shifting 𝚽n\boldsymbol\Phi_n by [1][1] leaves automorphism −1-1. A proposed identity binary map would then have source automorphism (−1)2=+1(-1)^2=+1 and target automorphism −1-1, so its intertwining equation would be c=−cc=-c. The base normalization is necessary even though its underlying complex is just a shift.

Downstairs choose Ln=Kℳ¯nL_n=K_{\overline{\mathcal M}_n}. For the quotient map ana_n, one has an*Ln=λn⊗det⁡Wa_n^*L_n=\lambda_n\otimes\det W, where W=Lie⁡(E)W=\operatorname{Lie}(E). The complete coefficient comparison is

p*(𝑲a⊠B𝑲b)[0]→∼q!𝑲a+b. p^*(\boldsymbol K_a\boxtimes_B\boldsymbol K_b)[0] \xrightarrow{\sim}q^!\boldsymbol K_{a+b}.

Equal dimensions alone would not supply this conclusion for arbitrary correspondences: the actual smooth substitution squares are used.

The paired orbit complex explains what translation reduction retains. A local matrix ZZ presenting a length-nn torsion sheaf gives, in endomorphism degrees 0,1,2,30,1,2,3,

𝔤𝔩n⊕W→(ad⁡Z,In)𝔤𝔩n→0𝔤𝔩n→(ad⁡Z,−Tr⁡)𝔤𝔩n⊕W*. \mathfrak{gl}_n\oplus W \xrightarrow{(\operatorname{ad}Z,I_n)}\mathfrak{gl}_n \xrightarrow0\mathfrak{gl}_n \xrightarrow{(\operatorname{ad}Z,-\operatorname{Tr})} \mathfrak{gl}_n\oplus W^*.

Collision fibres distinguish Hall traces and preserve relative centres

The comparison defines an associative unital algebra object A=⨁n≥0Rπn,*KnA=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}R\pi_{n,*}K_n in D(B;ℚ)D(B;\mathbb Q). Multiplication uses endpoint pullback, the comparison and proper trace along qq. The relative Künneth map follows after trivializing the torsor: the presentation [Qn/GLn][Q_n/\mathrm{GL}_n] has finite-dimensional rational cohomology in each degree and no negative cohomology, so each tensor degree has finitely many summands. Charge support is finite, but the global cohomology of a fixed charge need not be bounded. These are ordinary direct images, not compact integration over a nonproper sheaf stack.

Two length-one sheaves expose the collision coefficient. On the difference curve δ=e2−e1∈E\delta=e_2-e_1\in E, resolve one point sheaf and apply Hom to the other. This gives the global complex

D(ke1,ke2)=[𝒪E→s0𝒪E(0)]0,1, D(k_{e_1},k_{e_2})= [\mathcal O_E\xrightarrow{s_0}\mathcal O_E(0)]_{0,1},

[Ta,Pα]=−Pα−ea,[Ta,Qα]=−Qα−ea; [T_a,P_\alpha]=-P_{\alpha-e_a},\qquad [T_a,Q_\alpha]=-Q_{\alpha-e_a};

a negative index means zero. An energy-admissible module is a differential graded representation with nonnegative energy: its differential preserves energy, TaT_a raises it by one, and a charge of index α\alpha lowers it by |α|+1|\alpha|+1. Complete in an even parameter tt, requiring finite energy support at each coefficient of tt.

The exchange is

R2(z)=exp⁡(t∑α,γ∂α(−∂)γβ2(z)(Qα⊗Pγ−Pα⊗Qγ)). R_2(z)=\exp\!\left(t\sum_{\alpha,\gamma} \partial^\alpha(-\partial)^\gamma\beta_2(z) \bigl(Q_\alpha\otimes P_\gamma-P_\alpha\otimes Q_\gamma\bigr)\right).

The derivatives are undivided, forms precede operators, and the total tensor sign is retained. Every sum is finite on a fixed-energy input. The exchange theorem proves closedness, inverse exchange, Yang–Baxter, the block hexagons and horizontality on separated configurations. The degree-zero exponents commute, while the translation brackets differentiate their coefficients.

A concrete representation is 𝒫=ℂ[uα]⊗Λ(vα)\mathcal P=\mathbb C[u_\alpha]\otimes\Lambda(v_\alpha), with degrees |uα|=0|u_\alpha|=0, |vα|=1|v_\alpha|=1, zero differential and energy |α|+1|\alpha|+1 on either generator. Translation raises the index; Pα=∂uαP_\alpha=\partial_{u_\alpha} and Qα=∂vαQ_\alpha=\partial_{v_\alpha}. On u0⊗v0u_0\otimes v_0, the first exchange coefficient is −β2-\beta_2. The moment construction includes this polynomial representation into the supported Gaussian complex by an injective cochain map. It does not assert injectivity on cohomology. General compact smooth kernels can have infinitely many nonzero moments and are outside the energy-admissible domain proved here.

The zero-jet formula omits translation and belongs to the subalgebra generated by P0,Q0P_0,Q_0. It is not obtained by quotienting out higher jets while retaining TaT_a, since [Ta,Pea]=−P0[T_a,P_{e_a}]=-P_0. Finally, the native comparison still asks for a map to the completed cut-cobar realization and for extensions through derived collisions, preserving the central parameter, vacuum, ordered product and coproduct, including nonconsecutive channels. A separated exchange is a positive construction on its stated domain; those collision maps are additional data.

What is stable, and what remains to be determined

The strongest stable part of the picture is a network of explicit constructions with declared domains: geometric bar–cobar, full coefficient duality, marked field realization, spectral recognition, native first-order adjunction, free junction reconstruction, supported Wilson operations and several integral or analytic comparisons. These results give models on which a general formulation can be tested. The obstructions specify restrictions that such a formulation must explain.

The remaining uncertainty concerns the maps joining these constructions. The independently defined interacting field domain, the necessary marking, the comparison of geometric and physical actions, the completed local mapping category, the higher quantum tensor and the physically prepared state are different questions. Solving one can change the natural formulation of another, but no single unfinished arrow currently represents all of them.

Centres and physical bulk actions Ambient universal constructions, scoped factorizing nonfinality, full marked localization and the Heisenberg scalar and evaluation calculations The trace-complement localization fibre, the other marked comparisons, and a physical action category with its supported realization

Some questions have become better posed by separating a construction from a stronger claim formerly attached to it. The existence of a cochain actor is separate from its finality. Nonfinality by parallel maps is separate from the stronger two-object witness. A coefficient equivalence is separate from fixed-marking field reconstruction. A finite polewise calculation is separate from a continuous map through all energies. These distinctions preserve both the positive theorem and the harder question.

A common enhanced geometry could explain the carriers as presentations or restrictions. A formulation by boundaries and interfaces could make physical junctions primary. Comparison theorems on natural domains could preserve distinct constructions. Action categories and relative invariants could retain information without a universal representing object. These alternatives organize the remaining maps differently and may overlap. The evidence does not select a global formulation.

8Frontier relations

The comparisons and the maps they require

The graph follows the same target relations as the mathematical frontier. Choose a question or a difficulty family to see its neighbours. Every edge has a named relation and its exact scope below the diagram. A prerequisite belongs to its specified construction; a related question carries no implication.

Further comparison questions

These questions have distinct scopes. In particular, forgetting only a polynomial core differs from forgetting charge and jet markings as well; lifting a parallel pair differs from lifting a specified coherent loop.

NEW-01 · Compute the derived invariant of actions when no factorizing centre represents it
For a declared test category generated by the degree-two polynomial actor and finite exterior actors, construct a natural computational model of F↦Act(F,C_Q), with full mapping spaces and comparison fibres. Compute homotopy through degree two and its composition data, then state the exact extension to the full actor category. A category nerve or its realization does not replace this functor.
NEW-02 · Determine which prepared tests detect supported operation homotopies
Fix the relative supported operation complex at two and three positions, its lower operations and allowed counterterms. Construct the cochain evaluation Ev into the product or continuous end of independently prepared test complexes, with mixed insertions, endpoint and sewing maps; compute its homotopy fibre and the degrees in which it is conservative. If it fails, give an admissible derived enlargement of the preparation sector.
NEW-W1-01 · Physical admissibility of the native monoid obstruction
Construct R:P_C→Act_geom(C) from the independently defined abelian mixed BV bulk–boundary category on objects, morphisms and full action-comparison paths, preserving unit, product, both supported collision branches and higher coherences. Decide whether the source, recipient and both arrows of the specified parallel pair of transverse monoid actions lift together and whether its detector survives every physical receiving equalization.
NEW-W1-02 · Field realization independent of a current-core marking
Initially retain charge, weight and commuting jet actions, and forget only the polynomial current core from the full field systems. Define the intrinsic unmarked domain without presupposing it is the marked image; determine the groupoid of compatible cores and descend the realized coefficient functor with tensorators, vacuum triangles and all mapping-space coherences.
W1-NEW01 · Intrinsic recognition and descent of the charged-current field realization
Fix the full retained coefficient category, then forget the polynomial current core, charge and constituent-jet markings while retaining the complete collision algebra, geometric translation, density, empty unit, scalar-current projection and local vacuum operations. For every permitted continuous operation-preserving coefficient equivalence construct a coherent lift to the localized field category, or an invariant obstruction in its mapping-space fibre; recognize the essential image intrinsically and compatibly under R_(r+1)→R_r.
W1-NEW02 · Physical admissibility of the Heisenberg finality witness
For the exact pure abelian Chern–Simons half-space source with its action-defined junction at nonzero numerical level and hbar=1, construct PhysAct from regular finite-field smooth compact-kernel insertion families, polynomial dg parameters and admitted supported homotopies. Build P:PhysAct→Act_mon(C_Vk) on full mapping spaces, with products, collisions, incoming cap and vacuum compatibility; compute the lift fibre over the degree-two polynomial actor, its augmentation action and the complete coherent action loop. Prove any physical support/Ward obstruction stable under all allowed changes.

What could the completed theory look like?

The constructions leave several possible relationships between geometry, fields, boundaries and physical states. The possibilities below are not an exhaustive classification, and more than one can hold in different domains. Their purpose is to identify a map whose construction—or a counterexample to that same map—would change the mathematical picture.

A common enhanced geometric theory

One possibility is a geometric category rich enough to retain singular products, supported collisions, local vacua and all coherent corrections, with the word, atlas and field descriptions obtained by explicit functors. The associative bar construction and full coefficient anti-equivalence provide parts of this structure. Full-overlap exchange gives another part: changing charts must compare actual operations on their intersections.

The desired comparison cannot be the identity between the existing carriers. At three positions, the word support retains an outer collision with a distinct spectator. On the atlas, componentwise factorization and joint word factorization differ already at two distinct points. On full coefficients, transposition lands in pro-perfect diagrams. A common theory would explain these differences by its functors and their essential images.

Deciding comparison. Construct a functor from an independently specified field domain to the geometric coefficient category that preserves the full binary operation, translation, local vacuum, every collision map and the required continuous tensor. Prove its inverse on a stated essential image. Test the nonconsecutive collision and a nontrivial completed coefficient before extending the domain. A contradiction on one admitted object restricts that proposed common domain; it does not by itself exclude every enhanced category.

The marked charged-jet realization proves that such a programme is possible on a specified domain. Unrestricted removal of its marking now has a non-liftable coefficient automorphism, while the framed subcategory retains a positive reconstruction. A common theory must therefore retain the necessary framing, restrict its comparison maps, or construct a new exchange domain. The atlas-heart result also retains fields through bar, restriction and cut cobar; replacing that sequence by literal restriction loses the outer collision.

An interacting transverse source presents another test. A proposed two-sided insertion rule forces the exchange to be the identity. This is a conditional rigidity theorem: it applies only when both insertion identities hold, and those identities have not been established for every admissible interacting source. The corrected two-block homotopy evaluates its marked Hessian at the output after applying the Cauchy identity. Treating that Hessian as an internal pole-slot operator does not define the same global map. For the chosen pair homotopies, a three-block obstruction is already nonzero for the cubic potential yx2/2yx^2/2. The insertion theorem, the two-block construction and the fixed-pair obstruction retain these scopes. They neither refute every transverse realization nor show that every alternative pair homotopy fails. The physical interacting comparison remains open.

A theory organized by boundaries and interfaces

A second possibility takes boundary conditions and their junctions as the primary objects. Their bimodules recover algebras by derived endomorphisms; relative products describe fusion; caps evaluate states. The physical Wilson junction gives an action-derived example. The mode-level reverse derived-action equivalence gives a second, algebraically explicit example.

This organization makes locality a mathematical condition on maps of junctions. The sequence 2i2^i in the completed oscillator calculation shows that the full mode endomorphism algebra can exceed the image of local polynomial fields. A boundary theory can therefore reconstruct an algebra while leaving its local field realization open.

Deciding comparison. Define the boundary and junction independently from the bulk action, fix their coefficients, supports and completion, and compare their derived action with the proposed field algebra. Prove that composing junctions agrees with the native collision and fusion operations, including both vacua and supported contacts. For the abelian Wilson example, the supported cap comparison now provides the maps, contact homotopies and refinement compatibilities. Its further analytic extensions must retain the cap submodule and justify evaluation beyond the finite-orbit or finite-active-index domains.

This route also tests whether the bulk is determined by its action on the boundary. Its universal property is relative to the physical bulk–boundary category. The full geometric actor category has a nonfinality theorem, but transferring that theorem requires the realization of its obstructing maps. The boundary organization makes this missing functor explicit.

Several theories with precise comparison domains

A third possibility keeps several constructions with different coefficients, tensors or gradings and proves comparison theorems on their natural common domains. The examples already require this discipline. Squared Vandermonde multiplication identifies current-generated Hall subalgebras while their ambient integral polynomial lattices remain different. A bounded arithmetic division exists after a regularity shift while the original equal-regularity homotopy remains impossible. The internal line dual and coefficient dual each exist, but their vacuum comparisons cannot preserve every requested shift and operation simultaneously.

These are useful equivalences and useful distinctions. They are not evidence that every comparison must fail or that a single restricted recipient is the only possible formulation.

Deciding comparison. For each pair of constructions, specify carrier, coefficient ring, tensor, unit, variance, support and completion, then construct the map with the operations it preserves. State the hypotheses under which it is fully faithful, essentially surjective or an equivalence. Outside that domain, retain the first explicit defect and test whether it survives every replacement allowed by the question. A rational equivalence does not settle the integral question; an equality of exchange ratios does not settle the tensor question.

The linked question explorer collects these comparisons. Its missing maps are mathematical boundaries between constructions, rather than evidence that one historical list exhausts the subject.

A theory retaining nonrepresentability and relative obstructions

A fourth possibility treats the space of actions, the relative comparison complex or a defect category as the invariant, even when no final object represents it. The ordinary factorizing monoid-action theorem already forces this possibility on its declared actor class. The supported charge calculations illustrate the relative version: a particular shift has a nonzero cohomology detector, but the obstruction class for every admissible comparison still requires its full complex.

The positive constructions remain essential here. An ambient endomorphism object classifies actions in the larger category. A finite open gauge solves the charge comparison before support and continuity are imposed. Exact normal arrows and localization cubes retain extension data that intermediate images lose. These objects can organize the remaining problem without claiming a universal representative that has been disproved.

Deciding comparison. Construct the complete relative operation complex with the boundary conditions, topology, vacuum and normal maps fixed. Prove that its differential preserves the admissible cochains. Determine whether the actual comparison defect is a boundary, rather than testing only one chosen primitive. For a universal-action problem, determine the full mapping spaces in the intended category. A persistent parallel pair proves nonfinality; a claim about two objects without a common recipient requires that stronger witness separately.

The alternatives are distinguished by these maps and equations. A successful coefficient calculation can support several of them. The physical realization, tensor and state comparisons decide how far that calculation reaches.

9The open comparisons

The remaining questions and their deciding tests

The questions follow the constructions above. Each retains the strongest positive result already available and names the extra map that would extend it. A same-scope counterexample must use the original class of objects and permitted changes; failure of a narrower method does not decide the whole question.

Realizing the second algebra by fields

Open problem. Identify a natural domain on which the full associative coefficient dual is realized by independently specified covariant fields, with an operation-preserving equivalence. Retain both singular products, translation, the local vacuum extension, spectators, finite normal derivatives and the continuous tensor. The unrestricted forgetful comparison for the marked charged-jet domain has a non-liftable coefficient automorphism. Determine a natural restriction on its maps or the minimal framing that permits reconstruction, or construct a class with a new exchange mechanism. A negative answer for any further proposed domain must survive every replacement permitted in that domain.

The coefficient anti-equivalence and the marked current realization already exist. Transporting the marking preserves a positive comparison, and current framings have an explicit automorphism group. Computing either construction again does not make the forgotten core canonical or construct the first state–field map outside that domain. The comparison with quadratic chiral field duality must likewise identify full field systems, not only paired generators and quadratic relations.

For the rational 𝔤𝔩2\mathfrak{gl}_2 ghost construction, finite native adjunction is constructed classically and at first quantum order. Its kernel, full ghost mode data and finite perfect Spencer diagrams were defined in the results chapter. The native polar comparison now preserves both ordered residue products at first order on the universal vacuum carrier. The remaining question asks for its next quantum lift and its relation to fusion on an independently specified native module category.

The second-order lift and native module fusion

Open problem. Over R3=ℂ[ℏ]/(ℏ3)R_3=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^3), lift the constructed first-order native adjunction and its two ordered polar coefficient comparisons. Construct the second-order product, differential, curving and current change, reducing to the same comparison over R2=ℂ[ℏ]/(ℏ2)R_2=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^2). Retain coefficient biduality, arbitrary spectators, every finite normal derivative, both local vacua and the exchanged 13∣213\mid2 residue.

Construct the compatible three-input homotopies at this order and compare the result with fusion in an independently specified native module category. The first-order source is the universal native vacuum carrier with its finite compatible coefficient blocks; it is not identified with the ordinary tensor of two curved level-KK sources. A higher-order obstruction for one fixed ghost product decides its specified extension problem. A negative conclusion for the full field-realization problem must retain every replacement permitted there.

The first-order construction includes the full mixed differential and cofinal native block maps. Its finite right adjoint cancels the divergent coefficient of the direct relative twist before the cyclic limit is taken. The native polar comparison also supplies the full first-order exchanged residue diagram on its stated vacuum domain. The second-order lift, its three-input compatibility and the native module-fusion comparison remain open. For the nonlinear spin-three pair, the analogous first missing object is the binary configuration realization of its intrinsic restricted state dual; the raw-transpose and fixed-marking obstructions do not exhaust the allowed realizations.

At noncritical levels the specified fixed ghost product has no associative extension modulo ℏ4\hbar^4. That result concerns the fixed product and its allowed extension, not every possible replacement in the full field-realization problem. The next construction must state its admissible replacements before drawing a universal negative conclusion.

Extending an open comparison through the supported collision

Open problem. Construct the factorized target Taylor map and its actual module action for the two-point charge comparison, including the regular extension cochain. Compare its polynomial, finite-pole and open energy-completed diagrams coherently. Then determine the complete defect in the admissible continuous module-cochain complex, retaining the internal differential, finite Taylor action, residue and both connections. A positive answer must supply a relative primitive and module comparison on both ordered charts, preserving both singleton vacua and the normal gauge. For each independently fixed pole bound rr and transverse arity bb, the maps must be continuous through all field energies. A negative answer must detect a nonzero class after every admissible correction, not only after the Laurent shift or the finite open primitive already tested.

The finite numerical transfer in every arity, the open FπF\pi representative, the separate normal gauge, the finite open homotopy and the coherent residue are positive results. The residue commutator and the high-mode growth calculations explain why they do not automatically combine into the supported comparison. The next test is on the relative complex of the actual map.

Comparing physical and geometric actors

Open problem. Define the category of admissible physical bulk–boundary systems independently of a chosen boundary presentation, and construct its supported realization into factorizing transverse monoid actions on that boundary. The functor must retain mapping spaces, vacua, collisions and action-comparison homotopies. Decide whether the geometric non-equalizable parallel pair lifts. If it does, the geometric theorem excludes physical terminality on that class. If it does not, identify the missing admissibility or lifting condition and determine terminality in the physical category itself.

A positive geometric terminality comparison requires more than full faithfulness: the sufficient criterion proved above also requires generation of the geometric action category by colimits of physical actions. These are colimits preserving the action structure. The ambient endomorphism construction cannot be substituted for that hypothesis.

The polynomial Ward category gives a concrete restriction on such a proposal. Its nonzero one-root actions cannot map to factorizing actors, although that ordinary symmetry category has its own final object. A category of local bulk couplings must therefore be constructed from its actual supported operations; identifying it with those global Ward symmetries would change the comparison.

The stronger historical question about two action objects with the prescribed nonzero singleton vacuum and no common factorizing recipient remains separate. The split coalgebra with vanishing singleton has such a pair, but lies outside that vacuum-bearing class. The parallel-map theorem does not provide those objects. A solution must exhibit the two objects and rule out every common recipient, or prove an actual conversion of the parallel-pair witness into that stronger form.

Open problem. For the nonzero-level rank-one Heisenberg boundary, compute the derived functor F↦Act⁡(F,C)F\mapsto\operatorname{Act}(F,C) on a fixed test category of factorizing transverse actors. Begin with the degree-two polynomial actor and finite exterior actors, closed under their specified derived tensor operations. Construct a natural comparison with the actual action spaces and their mapping fibres, and calculate the homotopy groups through degree two together with composition. The full coherent loop and the obstruction to equalizing receiving maps must survive. Passing to singleton actions or connected components alone is a test that must fail; a nonrepresentable action functor is a meaningful possible answer.

Descent, locality and coherent fusion

Open problem. Extend the constructed geometric inverse image beyond the symmetric and regular square-zero incidence domains. The full marked sign-particle sector has effective descent for arbitrary étale covering families, including supported normal derivatives and both unit objects. General regular particle exchange has the double-cover Čech construction with independent-lift compatibility, but its mixed-component data need not be local. For an independently specified larger category, construct exchange and coherent collisions at distinct points with equal images, together with cuts, vacua and supported normal operations, and prove covering-family descent. Specify the source category and allowed equivalent replacements independently of the proposed functor.

The symmetric Heisenberg reconstruction, the regular nonidentity-exchange double-cover construction and the intrinsic sign-sector descent are positive results on their respective domains. The odd-pole example refutes the requested inverse-image comparison on the unrestricted class retaining its polar exchange and both ordered coproducts. Ordinary open-descent failure, the larger particle category’s missing mixed-component locality and failure of raw coefficient pullback are distinct obstructions. Outside the constructed domains, extending a binary exchange does not supply its higher collision coherences.

The finite directed-composition contraction is already proved for every finite number of inputs. The new Heisenberg Taylor/Wick seam coefficient also gives the supported comparison with the cut-refined residue complex in every finite arity, including four positions. The next geometric question uses nonidentity state exchange: construct its independent seam coefficient and compare all cuts, collisions, vacua and coherent support transports. Its proof needs a replacement for the mutually local acyclicity argument. Separately, a proposed comparison with prescribed lower homotopies must solve its full relative pentagon; the finite algebraic contraction alone supplies no such solution.

For local junctions, construct the full native curved mapping category and its evaluation comparison with the independently defined boundaries. The strict exterior-linear end contraction and its scalar support cubes are already available. The right-boundary-linear end instead has curvature, which must be retained in its mapping differential. Solve the evaluation homotopy on the three intersecting collision divisors with both boundaries, normal support and vacuum fixed. The torsion-free formal-ring theorem does not settle finite-precision specialization. For logarithmic probes, equip the exact normal arrows and complete localization cubes with coherent supported field substitutions so their derived maps agree with the zero-mode Koszul complexes under composition.

Quantum groups on a common recipient

Open problem. Construct a common supported category of modules for the spectral, categorical and geometric quantum-group descriptions. Give its tensorator, unit, exchange and associativity maps, with their collision extensions and coefficient topology. Compare them at the same level datum. For the field-valued Laurent recognition equations, establish natural hypotheses that guarantee solutions and an effective version at finite formal precision.

Three concrete domains now carry the relevant positive maps: finite-type trace modules have represented first-order native fusion with the full vacuum; the braided finite Heisenberg fibre reconstructs its charge action and interaction tensor; and standard evaluation words on a fixed logarithm strip admit a regular rigid tensor equivalence between Yangian and quantum-loop representations. Their coefficient spaces and completions differ. The common supported recipient must recover these operations on their own domains and prove the additional derived, collision and continuous-tensor comparisons required in the broader question.

Recognition criteria and the pro-reductive presentation results are positive theorems at their stated hypotheses. Local finiteness on the full Lie algebra and sufficient translation-stable finite quotients cannot be omitted from the latter. The horizontal-lift classification and its supported cotensor extension are constructed for the prescribed coherent rational action. They separate algebraic stabilization, constant-character translation equations and neutralization of the nonabelian factor system. Their concrete solution groupoids and comparisons with separately completed or physical recipients remain to be determined. Cases in which component groups move semisimple central elements retain their Laurent-gauge problem. The dg-shifted line structure also needs its own comparison with degree-zero spectral data.

The fixed Yangian-coproduct twist and literal Oq(GL2)O_q(GL_2) routes have scoped negative results. They leave enlarged, completed, categorical and geometric Hopf realizations available for investigation. A comparison after enlarging the level datum does not decide the original comparison at a fixed classical level.

Native Hall and elliptic operations

Open problem. Construct the oriented coefficient functor taking the intended critical Hall correspondences to the proposed chiral recipient. It must preserve extension products, the supported cooperation and its Euler interchange, both moment directions, right coefficient actions and the vacuum. Identify the normal Gysin map with the native operation through the required homotopy. If localization changes the supported detector, state and prove the support-moving comparison rather than identifying the localized object with the intrinsic one.

The Euler shuffle square, the current-generated integral equivalence and the conifold obstruction are all retained. The unresolved tensor is the ordinary all-charge one, beyond the torsion-free tensor image on which the positive theorem is proved.

Open problem. Realize the age- and parity-corrected elliptic coefficients by a global object with nonzero cycle-joining operations compatible with positive-weight field modes. Compare its bracket and compact Hall orientation with the proposed Igusa object, including the native modular normalization. Decide whether the changed all-height dg Lie presentation is geometrically realized. Equality of indices, the height-five differential and the ground-state joining formulas do not provide that object-level comparison.

The integral elliptic question additionally retains supersingular coefficients, operation-compatible base change and the spectral tensor. Agreement on every complex and Tate test is insufficient, as the square-zero module example proves.

Full-domain positivity and native arithmetic recoupling

Open problem. Prove positivity on a cofinal domain of the complete arithmetic test algebra, construct a negative test there, or construct an independently positive geometric state whose image reaches that full domain. The comparison must retain every prime-power term, both polar evaluations, the archimedean term and the arithmetic test topology. A recipient made positive by an assumption equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis does not provide an independent proof of it.

The density theorem and the bounded division on a shifted regularity scale supply better domains for comparison. They do not transfer positivity from finite matrices or narrow windows without control of the relevant topology. Infinite determinant sewing still needs the global trace-class estimate, including all intermediate support masks.

For arithmetic recoupling, identify the actual four-input associator carrier and its two residues, then compare it with the larger invertible junction network and its compression. A conditional detector requiring a particular value of the native zeroth residue remains conditional until that value is constructed. For the remaining standard-lattice finite-fusion example, period five is the next undecided ratio after the even-ratio theorem and the stated ratio-three calculation.

From a quantum action to a physical state

Open problem. On one independently specified Neumann, endpoint or gravity model, construct the action-derived insertion map and a local cyclic BV–BFV regulator. Compare their quantum operations in the actual local counterterm complex, retaining both normal-source insertions and boundary/corner transgression. Determine the first surviving relative anomaly after all permitted local corrections. Prove the resulting state and sewing maps, including the determinant line, vacuum phase and cap normalization.

The zero-source Gaussian, positive prescribed gravity density, finite all-jet Wilson operations and local Hamiltonian constructions are starting points for this comparison. Each has its own coefficient and support domain. A Hilbert-space interpretation, a Euclidean-to-Lorentzian reduction and topologization require their respective maps; none follows from positivity of a scalar density alone.

Open problem. At a fixed Heisenberg boundary, determine which independently prepared states and insertions detect supported operation homotopies. Specify a relative operation complex at two and three positions, holding lower operations and both vacua fixed, and construct its cochain evaluation into the actual scalar-filling or cap test complexes. Compute the homotopy fibre of this evaluation, with the prescribed continuity, bounded-pole and energy conditions. A nonzero operation class invisible to every admitted test disproves completeness of that family. Seek the smallest justified extension of the test complexes that detects it, preserving their preparation and sewing maps.

The distinction from state reconstruction is essential. The scalar filling law determines positive trace-class density operators, and mixed insertions distinguish the two states (p12±p2)/2(p_1^2\pm p_2)/2 that have identical one-mode laws. Neither fact says that equality of scalar evaluations supplies a cochain homotopy between supported operations. Deleting the mixed tests loses the first distinction; replacing every test complex by its degree-zero scalar values can lose the second.

The linked question explorer gives the additional formulations, examples and falsifiers. Where a question has been answered or its hypotheses revised, it gives the resulting theorem and preserves the original comparison’s scope.

10Distinctions that the examples force

The recurring mistakes and their corrections

The distinctions below apply throughout the mathematics, including to positive results. They explain why superficially similar formulas can answer different questions.

  1. Associative and Lie–commutative duality. The operads and the resulting structures differ. An envelope comparison relates them only on its proved domain.
  2. A resolution and a second algebra. Bar–cobar recovers the input. Producing another algebra requires the specified coefficient, field or internal duality.
  3. Lie-type examples and all examples. Curved commutative current duals do not imply commutativity for nonlinear relations or nonidentity exchange.
  4. Algebras and coalgebras. Strong separation maps give a coalgebra for cut convolution. Reversing their variance can kill the residue one intended to retain.
  5. The algebraic operad and its geometric operations. Associativity remains associativity; the geometric pseudo-tensor structure changes. On the unchanged diagonal differential-module domain, strict associative readings have the stated nilpotence restrictions.
  6. The ordered carrier and the transverse line. Both constructions are retained. Choosing the easier one does not prove their comparison.
  7. One sigma model and holography in general. Every bulk–boundary system has its own fields, observables, support and reconstruction map.
  8. A dg-shifted line algebra and a degree-zero spectral symmetry. A degree-one Maurer–Cartan element is not a degree-zero exchange. Their comparison must retain degree and carrier.
  9. A label and its current statement. A historical question label can identify a theorem today. Its actual environment and proof govern.
  10. An index and an operation-preserving map. Equal characters or scalar residues can hide different extensions, parity spaces and brackets. For example, a proposed dimension function taking values 77 and 66 on a module and its dual cannot come from a rigid monoidal functor.
  11. A presentation and its invariant category. A twist can change a Hopf presentation without changing the category. A question about a presentation must say which changes are permitted.
  12. A convention and a harmless sign. The binary coefficient is −1/κ-1/\kappa in the stated convention; reversed comodule tails transpose the form; odd-line shifts and the order of gauge pullbacks affect the maps.
  13. Formal and algebraic identities. A formal translation does not automatically preserve an algebraic subgroup or ideal. The relevant stability and topology must be proved.
  14. An insensitive check and a deciding test. A test must detect the proposed failure. Nonradial source profiles can retain an extra delta contact even when a radial computation has none.
  15. One failed recipe and a universal obstruction. A falsifier must survive every replacement admitted by the question.
  16. An obstruction and a verdict on the entire theory. A nonzero class can be an invariant of the proposed theory or evidence that its recipient must change. The same-scope calculation determines which inference is justified.
  17. A theorem and altered hypotheses. A proof establishes its stated claim. Changing the coefficient domain, allowed maps or completion requires a new argument.
  18. A theorem and a stronger concluding sentence. The conclusion must retain the theorem’s domain, hypotheses and quantifiers.
  19. A classical construction and a new claim. Classical results retain their attribution and hypotheses. Their application to a new coefficient or support domain requires its own comparison.
  20. An exact statement and a truncated excerpt. The complete environment, including every hypothesis and conclusion, is necessary. Full statements and proofs are supplied in the linked offline reference.
  21. A first step and the original question. A solved subproblem leaves every stronger unmet requirement visible. The result is assessed at the original mathematical criterion, rather than by the amount of preliminary calculation.

bfv

The BV formalism describes gauge fields, their symmetries and equations by a graded space with an odd Poisson bracket and a degree-one differential. In its quantum version an additional second-order operator Δ\Delta enters. The quantum master equation for an action SS is dS+12{S,S}+ℏΔS=0dS+\tfrac12\{S,S\}+\hbar\Delta S=0, with the stated degrees and regularization. The BFV boundary formalism equips boundary fields with their boundary symplectic and charge data so that restriction and gluing are compatible with the bulk equations.

A cyclic pairing is a specified bilinear pairing compatible with the differential and with cyclic permutation of inputs to the operations, including the degree signs. It is the extra datum that permits action functionals and gluing contractions in algebraic models. Its existence does not follow from multiplication alone.

Here is the derived category used by the comparison. The regular actions are equivalently coactions of an exterior or polynomial coalgebra. Over ℂ\mathbb C, call a complex of such comodules coacyclic if it belongs to the smallest triangulated subcategory generated by total complexes of short exact sequences and closed under arbitrary direct sums. The semiderived category used here inverts a module map when its cone, after forgetting the multiplying action, is coacyclic for the regular coalgebra. For a differential graded coefficient algebra RR, the coefficient-valued comparison keeps RR-linear maps but tests this coacyclicity after forgetting RR as well. A completion is taken with respect to a stated filtration or system of quotients, such as M̂=lim←mM/FmM\widehat M=\underset{\longleftarrow}{\lim}_m M/F^mM. convolution centre

A vacuum insertion inserts the specified local identity at a selected position, compatibly with translations, collisions and the operations under consideration. A pointed action is an action together with a specified point or vacuum and its required unit compatibility. A derived action retains the action maps and their coherent homotopies in the enhanced category; it is not determined by the induced action on cohomology.

A final object, also called a terminal object, is an object ZZ in a category with mapping spaces such that Map⁡(F,Z)\operatorname{Map}(F,Z) is contractible for every object FF. For a symmetric tensor, an E2E_2 algebra can be described as an associative algebra object in the category of associative algebras, with its coherent interchange. For the symmetric convolution ⋆\star and an associative algebra AA, an action of such an FF is a module structure F⋆A→AF\star A\to A in associative algebras. The convolution centre of AA is final among these actions, with all maps and action homotopies retained. Its tensor is ⋆\star and its unit is KK. It is a different universal property from that of transverse actions on a coalgebra through ⊗!\otimes^! and JJ.

Factorization means that coefficients over separated groups of positions are identified with the external products of their coefficients. A factorization coalgebra for the cut product is a coaugmented coalgebra for which each component

Cn|Up→(Cp⊠Cn−p)|UpC_n|_{U_p}\longrightarrow(C_p\boxtimes C_{n-p})|_{U_p}

coquasitriangular form

A coquasitriangular form describes exchange by a bilinear form on a Hopf algebra, so that its values on the tails of two coactions interchange the comodule factors. A spectral form allows this bilinear form to depend rationally on separation, with prescribed translation and reversal identities. The complete axioms below include both multiplicativity rules, their order convention, and the compatibility with the Hopf product. Merely choosing a rational function does not supply these axioms.

Definition

A unitary spectral form on a Hopf algebra

Let HH be a flat Hopf algebra over RR with bijective antipode and a derivation and coderivation TT satisfying εT=0\varepsilon T=0. Put a(z)=ezTaa(z)=e^{zT}a. The subscripts a1,a2a_1,a_2 denote coproduct components with the finite sum understood. All six identities are required.

A unitary spectral coquasitriangular form on HH is an RR-bilinear map ρz:H⊗H→R[z,z−1]\rho_z\colon H\otimes H\to R[z,z^{-1}] with the following properties: ρz(1,a)=ε(a)=ρz(a,1),ρz(ab,c)=ρz(a,c1)ρz(b,c2),ρz(a,bc)=ρz(a1,c)ρz(a2,b),ρz(a1,b1)a2(z)b2=b1a1(z)ρz(a2,b2),ρz(Ta,b)=∂zρz(a,b)=−ρz(a,Tb),ρz(a1,b1)ρ−z(b2,a2)=ε(a)ε(b).\begin{align} \rho_z(1,a)&=\varepsilon(a)=\rho_z(a,1), \\ \rho_z(ab,c)&=\rho_z(a,c_1)\rho_z(b,c_2), \\ \rho_z(a,bc)&=\rho_z(a_1,c)\rho_z(a_2,b), \\ \rho_z(a_1,b_1)a_2(z)b_2 &=b_1a_1(z)\rho_z(a_2,b_2), \\ \rho_z(Ta,b)&=\partial_z\rho_z(a,b)=-\rho_z(a,Tb), \\ \rho_z(a_1,b_1)\rho_{-z}(b_2,a_2) &=\varepsilon(a)\varepsilon(b). \end{align} The fourth displayed identity is an identity in H[[z]][z−1]H[[z]][z^{-1}]. The order of the two factors in the third displayed identity is part of the convention.

cyclic pairing

The BV formalism describes gauge fields, their symmetries and equations by a graded space with an odd Poisson bracket and a degree-one differential. In its quantum version an additional second-order operator Δ\Delta enters. The quantum master equation for an action SS is dS+12{S,S}+ℏΔS=0dS+\tfrac12\{S,S\}+\hbar\Delta S=0, with the stated degrees and regularization. The BFV boundary formalism equips boundary fields with their boundary symplectic and charge data so that restriction and gluing are compatible with the bulk equations.

A cyclic pairing is a specified bilinear pairing compatible with the differential and with cyclic permutation of inputs to the operations, including the degree signs. It is the extra datum that permits action functionals and gluing contractions in algebraic models. Its existence does not follow from multiplication alone.

deformation quantization

A coisson algebra is the classical chiral Poisson structure: a commutative differential algebra with a singular Lie bracket satisfying the translation, skew-symmetry, Jacobi and Leibniz identities. In one coordinate the singular bracket is encoded by the polynomial λ\lambda-bracket {aλb}\{a_\lambda b\}. A deformation quantization is a flat formal deformation whose commutator, divided by its parameter and reduced at parameter zero, recovers that Poisson bracket, with the corresponding operation identities.

derived category

The derived category identifies quasi-isomorphic complexes; here an enhancement also retains their mapping complexes and coherent homotopies. A mapping space records maps, homotopies between maps, and higher homotopies. Its set of connected components alone is insufficient for specifying a coherently associative action. The heart for the usual cohomological grading consists of objects whose cohomology is concentrated in degree zero.

The derived tensor product M⊗R𝕃NM\otimes_R^{\mathbb L}N is computed by replacing a factor with a resolution whose tensor product preserves quasi-isomorphisms. It retains the extra cohomology that ordinary tensoring can lose. For instance, over R=k[u]R=k[u], the resolution [R→uR][R\xrightarrow{u}R] of k=R/(u)k=R/(u) gives k⊗R𝕃k=[k→0k]k\otimes_R^{\mathbb L}k=[k\xrightarrow{0}k], with nonzero terms in degrees −1-1 and 00.

Factorization means that coefficients over separated groups of positions are identified with the external products of their coefficients. A factorization coalgebra for the cut product is a coaugmented coalgebra for which each component

Cn|Up→(Cp⊠Cn−p)|UpC_n|_{U_p}\longrightarrow(C_p\boxtimes C_{n-p})|_{U_p}

is an equivalence, coherently under further cuts. It is also called strong. This condition is imposed on each specified separating map; a statement about the sum of several components can be different.

Introduced in Definitions and geometry

fat point

The quotient has the RR-basis 1,q1,q21,q_1,q_2. When ℏ\hbar is invertible it describes three distinct points. At ℏ=0\hbar=0 it becomes k[q1,q2]/(q1,q2)2k[q_1,q_2]/(q_1,q_2)^2, a fat point: one point together with the two first-order directions retained by its nilpotent coordinates. Replacing it by the reduced point would discard two of the three basis vectors. The general boundary-ideal theorem gives the analogous free quotient for every arity and boundary, using falling factorials in steps of ℏ\hbar.

Introduced in The whole mathematical picture

fibre functor

Over a field kk, a fibre functor on a kk-linear abelian monoidal category 𝒞\mathcal C is an exact faithful kk-linear strong monoidal functor F:𝒞→Vect⁡kfdF:\mathcal C\to\operatorname{Vect}^{\mathrm{fd}}_k, where the recipient consists of finite-dimensional vector spaces. Exactness preserves short exact sequences, and faithfulness means that the map on each space of morphisms is injective. The tensor and unit comparisons are isomorphisms; preservation of a symmetry is an additional requirement. Forgetting the action on a finite-dimensional group representation is an example.

Introduced in Definitions and geometry

Related

  • monoidal functor

field realization

A field realization expresses the relevant geometric algebra or module through states, translation and operator fields, preserving the specified operations. The matrix algebra of all continuous modes can be larger than the algebra realized by local fields. Thus double-centralizer reconstruction at the mode level and local field reconstruction are separate assertions.

Introduced in Definitions and geometry

Related

final object

A vacuum insertion inserts the specified local identity at a selected position, compatibly with translations, collisions and the operations under consideration. A pointed action is an action together with a specified point or vacuum and its required unit compatibility. A derived action retains the action maps and their coherent homotopies in the enhanced category; it is not determined by the induced action on cohomology.

A final object, also called a terminal object, is an object ZZ in a category with mapping spaces such that Map⁡(F,Z)\operatorname{Map}(F,Z) is contractible for every object FF. For a symmetric tensor, an E2E_2 algebra can be described as an associative algebra object in the category of associative algebras, with its coherent interchange. For the symmetric convolution ⋆\star and an associative algebra AA, an action of such an FF is a module structure F⋆A→AF\star A\to A in associative algebras. The convolution centre of AA is final among these actions, with all maps and action homotopies retained. Its tensor is ⋆\star and its unit is KK. It is a different universal property from that of transverse actions on a coalgebra through ⊗!\otimes^! and JJ.

formal

The modes above are the coefficients of fields. The notation also records which infinite expressions are admitted. A formal series is used through its coefficients and the operations defined on them; no numerical convergence is asserted. In V((z))V((z)) each vector-valued Laurent series has a finite lower bound on its powers of zz. The bound can depend on the input state.

Introduced in Basic examples

formal bound profile

A formal bound profile fixes pole order, weight transfer and finite matrix-degree bounds for each finite-input operation and each specified coherence cell. Require finite free scalar cells on finite weight blocks, and finite differential-module presentations of the whole collision diagram, including its actual normal relations. If every differential, support map, identity and coherence equation is a finite algebraic expression on each cell, a compatible framed system satisfying one common profile has a unique formal lift. Each matrix coefficient lifts to RR; separation proves the equations. The bounded-presentation proposition retains the pro-perfect test diagrams as diagrams. Recognizing an independently defined native category and all its mapping spaces from this presentation is a further theorem.

Introduced in The whole mathematical picture

formal parameter

A completion is taken with respect to a stated filtration or system of quotients, such as M̂=lim←mM/FmM\widehat M=\underset{\longleftarrow}{\lim}_m M/F^mM. A formal parameter ℏ\hbar specifies the quotients by ℏm\hbar^m. For a topologically free field module the target can be lim←m(V/ℏmV)((z))\underset{\longleftarrow}{\lim}_m(V/\hbar^mV)((z)): the allowed pole bound is finite at each precision, but need not be uniform in mm.

A continuous dual consists of linear maps continuous for the stated topology on the source and target. It depends on those topologies. A dual formed degree by degree under finite-dimensionality hypotheses, a continuous dual of a completed space, and a pro-object of finite duals are distinct constructions unless a comparison is supplied.

fusion

A junction is a meeting of specified boundary or line conditions. Algebraically its observables can form a bimodule MM carrying compatible actions of the algebras on its two sides. Morita comparison uses such bimodules to compare module categories. A double-centralizer equivalence identifies an algebra with the derived endomorphisms of MM over the algebra acting on the other side, with the appropriate opposite multiplication.

Fusion combines adjacent defects or boundary modules by a specified relative product; an algebraic model is M⊗B𝕃NM\otimes_B^{\mathbb L}N. Sewing requires these products and evaluations to agree when intervals or surfaces are glued. An incoming cap supplies the specified map or functional at an incoming boundary end. Its coefficient domain and compatibility with gluing are part of its definition.

hall operations

Hall operations use correspondences of extensions or flags: pull coefficients to a space of extensions, then push them to the middle object, with the required orientation and degree shifts. A critical locus of a function WW is the locus dW=0dW=0, with a derived version retaining its equations and relations. Vanishing cycles are the sheaf-theoretic coefficients that detect how fibres of WW change at its critical values. A critical Hall theory uses these coefficients and their orientation data; replacing its potential by zero changes the theory.

Introduced in Constructions and obstructions

heart

The derived category identifies quasi-isomorphic complexes; here an enhancement also retains their mapping complexes and coherent homotopies. A mapping space records maps, homotopies between maps, and higher homotopies. Its set of connected components alone is insufficient for specifying a coherently associative action. The heart for the usual cohomological grading consists of objects whose cohomology is concentrated in degree zero.

The derived tensor product M⊗R𝕃NM\otimes_R^{\mathbb L}N is computed by replacing a factor with a resolution whose tensor product preserves quasi-isomorphisms. It retains the extra cohomology that ordinary tensoring can lose. For instance, over R=k[u]R=k[u], the resolution [R→uR][R\xrightarrow{u}R] of k=R/(u)k=R/(u) gives k⊗R𝕃k=[k→0k]k\otimes_R^{\mathbb L}k=[k\xrightarrow{0}k], with nonzero terms in degrees −1-1 and 00.

A Heisenberg group is the central extension associated to a symplectic pairing, with multiplication (v,t)(w,s)=(v+w,t+s+12ω(v,w))(v,t)(w,s)=(v+w,t+s+\tfrac12\omega(v,w)) in characteristic zero. intervening field

An intervening field is an input whose ordered position lies between the two inputs being merged. To merge nonadjacent inputs, the earlier field is exchanged past each intervening field before its principal part is taken at the later input. The intervening fields remain present, and their passage operators can change the resulting residue.

The derived category identifies quasi-isomorphic complexes; here an enhancement also retains their mapping complexes and coherent homotopies. A mapping space records maps, homotopies between maps, and higher homotopies. Its set of connected components alone is insufficient for specifying a coherently associative action. The order of the two factors in the third displayed identity is part of the convention.

The Hopf algebra HH, translation TT and form ρz\rho_z are fixed as above. The word level in this general definition means an automorphism preserving these data. This includes families whose scalar current level is encoded by the chosen automorphism.

A level is a Hopf automorphism η\eta of HH such that ηT=Tη\eta T=T\eta and ρz(ηa,ηb)=ρz(a,b)\rho_z(\eta a,\eta b)=\rho_z(a,b). Levels form a group under composition, with η1η2=η1∘η2\eta_1\eta_2=\eta_1\circ\eta_2.

A spectral presentation of chiral symmetry

Here kk has characteristic zero, RR is a commutative kk-algebra, and the curve is the affine line with coordinate zz. The spectral-form axioms and level group have been displayed in full above. All Hopf algebras in this definition are in cohomological degree zero.

A spectral chiral quantum group over RR consists of the following data.

Definition

The category with translation and spectral exchange

A presentation is a monoidal equivalence with finite projective comodules of a flat Hopf algebra with bijective antipode, with the union condition for flat comodules stated above. Formal families and their finite-pole morphisms are interpreted coefficientwise. The translation acts on objects and morphisms, so both sides of each identity have the stated positioned source and target.

quantum master equation

The BV formalism describes gauge fields, their symmetries and equations by a graded space with an odd Poisson bracket and a degree-one differential. In its quantum version an additional second-order operator Δ\Delta enters. The quantum master equation for an action SS is dS+12{S,S}+ℏΔS=0dS+\tfrac12\{S,S\}+\hbar\Delta S=0, with the stated degrees and regularization. The BFV boundary formalism equips boundary fields with their boundary symplectic and charge data so that restriction and gluing are compatible with the bulk equations.

A cyclic pairing is a specified bilinear pairing compatible with the differential and with cyclic permutation of inputs to the operations, including the degree signs. It is the extra datum that permits action functionals and gluing contractions in algebraic models. Its existence does not follow from multiplication alone.

A quantum vertex algebra replaces ordinary locality by an exchange rule: reversing two insertions applies a specified operator 𝒮(z)\mathcal S(z) to their states. Subscripts such as 𝒮13\mathcal S_{13} mean that it acts on the first and third factors and leaves the second fixed. The following definition fixes the coefficient ring, the Laurent condition and the compatibility with products. The vacuum, translation and weak-associativity axioms referred to in it are the ones just stated.

The abbreviation dg means differential graded. A differential graded algebra is a cochain complex with associative multiplication of degree zero, a unit, and d(ab)=d(a)b+(−1)|a|ad(b)d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^{|a|}a\,d(b). A homotopy between cochain maps f,gf,g is a map hh of degree −1-1 satisfying f−g=dh+hdf-g=dh+hd. A quasi-isomorphism is a cochain map inducing isomorphisms on every cohomology group.

semiderived category

Here is the derived category used by the comparison. The regular actions are equivalently coactions of an exterior or polynomial coalgebra. Over ℂ\mathbb C, call a complex of such comodules coacyclic if it belongs to the smallest triangulated subcategory generated by total complexes of short exact sequences and closed under arbitrary direct sums. Forming a triangulated subcategory allows shifts and cones as well as isomorphisms. The semiderived category used here inverts a module map when its cone, after forgetting the multiplying action, is coacyclic for the regular coalgebra. For a differential graded coefficient algebra RR, the coefficient-valued comparison keeps RR-linear maps but tests this coacyclicity after forgetting RR as well. This last convention is essential for nonsplit coefficient localization sequences. The complete definition and derived action theorem supply the mapping complexes in that category.

sewing

A junction is a meeting of specified boundary or line conditions. Algebraically its observables can form a bimodule MM carrying compatible actions of the algebras on its two sides. Morita comparison uses such bimodules to compare module categories. A double-centralizer equivalence identifies an algebra with the derived endomorphisms of MM over the algebra acting on the other side, with the appropriate opposite multiplication.

Fusion combines adjacent defects or boundary modules by a specified relative product; an algebraic model is M⊗B𝕃NM\otimes_B^{\mathbb L}N. Sewing requires these products and evaluations to agree when intervals or surfaces are glued. An incoming cap supplies the specified map or functional at an incoming boundary end. Its coefficient domain and compatibility with gluing are part of its definition.

spectral form

A coquasitriangular form describes exchange by a bilinear form on a Hopf algebra, so that its values on the tails of two coactions interchange the comodule factors. A spectral form allows this bilinear form to depend rationally on separation, with prescribed translation and reversal identities. The complete axioms below include both multiplicativity rules, their order convention, and the compatibility with the Hopf product. Merely choosing a rational function does not supply these axioms.

superdimension

For a finite super vector space V=Veven⊕VoddV=V_{\mathrm{even}}\oplus V_{\mathrm{odd}}, its superdimension is dim⁡Veven−dim⁡Vodd\dim V_{\mathrm{even}}-\dim V_{\mathrm{odd}}. Internal parity and cohomological degree are separate gradings; total parity is their sum modulo two. An Euler or supercharacter identity records an alternating count and does not construct a graded object or an operation on it.

suspension

The suspension of a cochain complex here is sV=V[1]sV=V[1], so ss has degree −1-1. An A-infinity algebra has operations mnm_n of degree 2−n2-n whose identities express associativity with all coherent corrections. Equivalently, the corresponding degree-one coderivation on the tensor coalgebra of sVsV squares to zero. The first identity is m12=0m_1^2=0; the next says that m1m_1 is compatible with m2m_2; the next allows the associator of m2m_2 to be the differential of m3m_3.
