T

étale map

A change of curve can separate positions whose images coincide. For the map f:𝔾m→𝔾mf:\mathbb G_m\to\mathbb G_m, f(t)=t2f(t)=t^2, the points aa and −a-a are distinct when a≠0a\ne0, but have the same image. Pulling a source collision coefficient back to that pair need not produce the tensor product required at two distinct target points. An étale map between smooth complex curves is an algebraic map without ramification: its derivative in local parameters is invertible. This local condition permits several distinct points over one image. A descent theorem must reconstruct the target operations at such configurations and then show how compatible local objects and maps glue.

tensor product

To state exchange relations, one must keep the two inputs independent. The tensor product V⊗RWV\otimes_R W over a commutative ring RR represents bilinear maps from V×WV\times W that balance the two RR-actions. A flat RR-module is one for which tensoring preserves exact sequences. Unless a topology is specified, the tensor product here is algebraic: its elements are finite sums of elementary tensors.

Introduced in Basic examples

tensorator

A monoidal category has a tensor, a unit and coherent associativity and unit isomorphisms. A monoidal functor preserves them with coherent comparison maps. Its tensorator is the specified comparison between F(M)⊗F(N)F(M)\otimes F(N) and F(M⊗N)F(M\otimes N); for a strong monoidal functor it is an isomorphism. Naturality requires this comparison to commute with every admitted morphism, not just with the action on a chosen generator.

Introduced in Definitions and geometry

topologization

Topologization here means an additional construction making the chosen directional translations null-homotopic, with homotopies compatible with the operations and boundaries. Forgetting a coordinate or observing an invariant index does not supply it. The planar-oper, principal-chiral-model and all-spin-line comparisons, as well as the global torus dictionary, retain this requirement. The physical reconstruction still needs the renormalized current and ghost insertion, the regulator and determinant-line comparison, the endpoint complex, and the boundary/corner map from Euclidean preparation to Lorentzian evolution. A Lorentzian instability cannot be transferred across that last map before it is constructed.

Introduced in Constructions and obstructions

transverse monoid

At fixed holomorphic position, two insertions can still be ordered along a transverse real line. On coefficient systems the corresponding tensor is F⊗!G=Δ!(F⊠G)F\otimes^!G=\Delta^!(F\boxtimes G), with dualizing unit JJ. It combines coefficients at the same positions. The convolution ⋆\star combines coefficients of separate labelled blocks and has empty unit KK.

The forward interchange

(F⋆G)⊗!(H⋆L)→(F⊗!H)⋆(G⊗!L)(F\star G)\otimes^!(H\star L)\longrightarrow(F\otimes^!H)\star(G\otimes^!L)

projects onto summands with matching decompositions. It makes coaugmented convolution coalgebras a symmetric monoidal category for ⊗!\otimes^!, with unit JJ. The reverse inclusion exists in positive arities, but their composite on the larger sum is a projection, not the identity.

A transverse monoid is the associative algebra object for this second tensor. Its vacuum is a map from JJ, hence a compatible vacuum at every configuration. The full definition also fixes its actions.

Definition

The product at one holomorphic position

Let Coalg\mathrm{Coalg} denote coaugmented, counital convolution coalgebras with empty coefficient kk. Their diagonal tensor is ⊗!\otimes^!, their unit is the dualizing coalgebra JJ, and the forward interchange is the common-decomposition projection described above. This category includes the coherent maps used in the definition.

A transverse monoid is an associative algebra object of the symmetric monoidal category (Coalg⁡,⊗!,J)(\operatorname{Coalg},\mathbin{\otimes^!},J), in the sense of Jacob Lurie, Higher Algebra, Definition 4.1.1.6. It consists of a coalgebra F∈CoalgF\in\operatorname{Coalg} and maps of coalgebras m:F⊗!F→F,u:J→F,m\colon F\mathbin{\otimes^!}F\longrightarrow F,\qquad u\colon J\longrightarrow F, with coherent associativity and unit constraints. A transverse comonoid is a coassociative coalgebra object (G,∇,e)(G,\nabla,e) of the same category, with maps of coalgebras ∇:G→G⊗!G\nabla\colon G\to G\mathbin{\otimes^!}G and e:G→Je\colon G\to J. Let FF be a transverse monoid and C∈CoalgC\in\operatorname{Coalg}. A transverse action of FF on CC is a left FF-module structure α:F⊗!C→C\alpha\colon F\mathbin{\otimes^!}C\to C in this category Lurie, Higher Algebra, Definition 4.2.1.13.

V

vacuum insertion

A vacuum insertion inserts the specified local identity at a selected position, compatibly with translations, collisions and the operations under consideration. A pointed action is an action together with a specified point or vacuum and its required unit compatibility. A derived action retains the action maps and their coherent homotopies in the enhanced category; it is not determined by the induced action on cohomology.

A final object, also called a terminal object, is an object ZZ in a category with mapping spaces such that Map⁡(F,Z)\operatorname{Map}(F,Z) is contractible for every object FF. For a symmetric tensor, an E2E_2 algebra can be described as an associative algebra object in the category of associative algebras, with its coherent interchange. For the symmetric convolution ⋆\star and an associative algebra AA, an action of such an FF is a module structure F⋆A→AF\star A\to A in associative algebras. The convolution centre of AA is final among these actions, with all maps and action homotopies retained. Its tensor is ⋆\star and its unit is KK. It is a different universal property from that of transverse actions on a coalgebra through ⊗!\otimes^! and JJ.

vanishing cycles

Hall operations use correspondences of extensions or flags: pull coefficients to a space of extensions, then push them to the middle object, with the required orientation and degree shifts. A critical locus of a function WW is the locus dW=0dW=0, with a derived version retaining its equations and relations. Vanishing cycles are the sheaf-theoretic coefficients that detect how fibres of WW change at its critical values. A critical Hall theory uses these coefficients and their orientation data; replacing its potential by zero changes the theory.

P†=(RHom⁡D(P,D))t[d],t(f)=f,t(∂i)=−∂i,t(PQ)=t(Q)t(P).P^\dagger=(R\operatorname{Hom}_D(P,D))^t[d],\qquad t(f)=f,\quad t(\partial_i)=-\partial_i,\quad t(PQ)=t(Q)t(P).

The canonical line makes this independent of a coordinate volume. On holonomic differential modules, Verdier duality is the functor given by this derived-Hom formula, with the canonical-line conversion and dimension shift displayed above. It exchanges direct-image extension with its dual extension. The finite-cell operation extends the differential-module duality to a larger recipient: for M=colim⁡αPαM=\operatorname{colim}_\alpha P_\alpha, retain the entire pro-diagram M♯={Pα†}αM^\sharp=\{P_\alpha^\dagger\}_\alpha. A pro-diagram includes all stages and transition maps; it is not its ordinary inverse limit.
